accepted.s: Which one of the following schemes is specifically aimed at meritorious girls of Classes IX–XII to address the under-representation of women in STEM?
accepted.x: Vigyan Jyoti targets meritorious girls of Classes IX–XII and seeks to address the under-representation of women in STEM. It is implemented by DST through the agency Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.
accepted.tq: Direct target-group discrimination among closely related women-in-science schemes.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding WISE-KIRAN:
1. It is associated with the Department of Science and Technology.
2. It particularly supports women scientists who have experienced a career break.
3. Its programmes include WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. WISE-KIRAN is a DST initiative for women scientists, especially those with career breaks, and includes WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI.
accepted.tq: Statement combination using the common body, target group and component relationship.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s: WIDUSHI, associated with WISE-KIRAN, is intended primarily for which of the following groups?
o: Women scientists seeking their first extramural biotechnology grant
Senior women scientists conducting interdisciplinary research in science and technology
accepted.x: WIDUSHI is meant for senior women scientists engaged in interdisciplinary research in science and technology.
accepted.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between WIDUSHI, BioCARe, GATI and Vigyan Jyoti.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s: GATI is best described as a programme that:
o: Offers fellowships to doctoral students in natural sciences
Promotes gender-equity charters in institutions and is modelled on the UK's Athena SWAN
Provides short-term research visits for overseas scientists
Provides grants to women scientists in biotechnology after a career break
accepted.x: GATI stands for Gender Advancement for Transforming Institutions. It promotes institutional gender equity through a charter modelled on the UK's Athena SWAN.
accepted.tq: Purpose-based identification of an institutional gender-equity programme.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SERB-POWER — Women researchers in academic and R&D institutions
GATI — Women scientists returning to India from abroad
Vigyan Jyoti — Senior interdisciplinary women scientists
accepted.x: SERB-POWER provides research grants and fellowships to women researchers in academic and R&D institutions. GATI, BioCARe and Vigyan Jyoti have the other stated purposes incorrectly assigned.
accepted.tq: Find the sure scheme-target pair and reject swapped beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s: BioCARe is a DBT initiative that primarily supports:
o: Senior scientists recognised for excellence in research
School students aged 10–15 with innovative ideas
Women scientists, mainly unemployed or career-break scientists, in biotechnology
accepted.x: BioCARe is a DBT programme for women scientists in biotechnology, particularly unemployed women or those returning after a career break. It provides the first extramural grant.
accepted.tq: Direct body-and-target matching with nearby scheme distractors.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s: As reported for 2026, approximately how many girls had been covered under Vigyan Jyoti?
accepted.x: Vigyan Jyoti had covered more than 29,000 girls according to the cited 2026 figure.
accepted.tq: Numerical recall using distinct programme-related figures.
accepted.sec: Women in science schemes → target group

accepted.s: INSPIRE was launched in 2008 by which organisation as a flagship programme?
accepted.x: INSPIRE, or Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research, is a flagship programme of the Department of Science and Technology launched in 2008.
accepted.tq: Direct year-and-agency recall.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its full form and target group?
o: SEATS — Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science — school students
SHE — Support for Her Education — doctoral researchers
AORC — Assured Opportunity for Research Careers — only school students
MANAK — Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge — university teachers
accepted.x: SEATS means Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science and targets school students. SHE is Scholarship for Higher Education, AORC concerns doctoral and post-doctoral careers, and MANAK concerns school students in Classes VI–X.
accepted.tq: Full-form trap using familiar-looking but incorrect expansions.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s: MANAK under INSPIRE is intended for students who are:
o: In Classes VI–X and generally aged 10–15 years
In Classes I–V and aged 6–10 years
accepted.x: MANAK targets students of Classes VI–X in the age group of approximately 10–15 years.
accepted.tq: Direct age-and-class range discrimination.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about INSPIRE components:
1. SHE stands for Scholarship for Higher Education.
2. SHE supports top-ranked students in undergraduate and postgraduate natural and basic sciences.
3. AORC includes the INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty programmes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. SHE is the higher-education scholarship component, while AORC covers research-career opportunities through INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty.
accepted.tq: Component-scope statement testing with a look-alike expansion trap.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s: In the context of INSPIRE, the acronym AORC refers to:
accepted.x: AORC stands for Assured Opportunity for Research Careers and includes the INSPIRE Fellowship for PhD scholars and INSPIRE Faculty support.
accepted.tq: Exact official-word discrimination among similar expansions.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s: In 2025, the MANAK programme recorded approximately 8.54 lakh ideas and gave ₹10,000 each to how many students?
accepted.x: In 2025, MANAK recorded 8.54 lakh ideas and awarded ₹10,000 each to 46,926 students.
accepted.tq: Figure-pair recall linking an amount with its beneficiary count.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the 2025 INSPIRE Fellowship is correct?
o: It was restricted to former MANAK awardees.
It provided 46,926 fellowships, all to school students.
It received only 653 applications for the INSPIRE Faculty call.
It provided 653 doctoral fellowships, of which 65% were awarded to female candidates.
accepted.x: The 2025 INSPIRE Fellowship provided 653 doctoral fellowships, and 65% of the recipients were female. Around 31% were former SHE scholars.
accepted.tq: Separating fellowship awards from application and school-innovation figures.
accepted.sec: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Ramanujan Fellowship?
o: It supports school students with innovative ideas
It supports senior scientists through an excellence grant only
It supports institutions adopting gender-equity charters
It supports Indian scientists abroad who return to India
accepted.x: The Ramanujan Fellowship, administered by SERB and now under ANRF, is intended to attract Indian scientists working abroad back to India.
accepted.tq: Brain-gain scheme identification by target group.
accepted.sec: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → target group and awarding body

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship — Indian life-science and biotechnology scientists abroad — DBT
VAJRA — Overseas scientists, including NRIs and OCIs — SERB/ANRF
J.C. Bose Fellowship — Active senior scientists recognised for excellence — SERB/ANRF
PMRF — Women scientists returning after a career break — Department of Biotechnology
accepted.x: PMRF is for PhD scholars in IITs, IISc, IISERs and other top institutions and is administered by the Ministry of Education. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly assigned target group and awarding body.
accepted.sec: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → target group and awarding body

accepted.s:
Which of the following schemes are identified with the objective of converting brain drain into brain gain?
1. VAJRA
2. Ramanujan Fellowship
3. INSPIRE
4. FIST
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: VAJRA, the Ramanujan Fellowship and INSPIRE are identified as brain-gain schemes. FIST is a DST infrastructure-upgradation programme, not a brain-gain fellowship.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the infrastructure programme from a target-group list.
accepted.sec: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → target group and awarding body

accepted.s: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship was begun in connection with:
o: The centenary of the Indian Science Congress
accepted.x: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship began in 1997 to mark 50 years of India’s Independence and supports young scientists with a proven record.
accepted.tq: Date-event association using a commemorative milestone.
accepted.sec: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → target group and awarding body

accepted.s: PMRF is primarily intended for PhD scholars in which of the following institutions?
o: IITs, IISc, IISERs and other top institutions
accepted.x: The Prime Minister’s Research Fellows scheme supports PhD scholars in IITs, IISc, IISERs and other top institutions. It was introduced in 2018.
accepted.tq: Institutional eligibility discrimination.
accepted.sec: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → target group and awarding body

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its purpose?
o: PURSE — Grants based on university research-publication performance
SAIF — Scholarships for school students in science
FIST — Upgrading laboratories and infrastructure in higher educational institutions
SATHI — Shared and professionally managed infrastructure with costly instruments
accepted.x: SAIF means Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facilities and provides access to high-end instruments through regional centres. Scholarships for school students are not its purpose.
accepted.tq: Purpose-based elimination of an unrelated scholarship description.
accepted.sec: DST facility programmes - full forms and purpose

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I
(a) SATHI
(b) FIST
(c) PURSE
(d) SAIF

List-II
(i) Grants based on research-publication performance
(ii) Regional access to high-end analytical instruments
(iii) Shared professionally managed S&T infrastructure
(iv) Laboratory and infrastructure upgrading in departments
accepted.x: SATHI provides shared infrastructure, FIST upgrades laboratories, PURSE uses research-publication performance for grants, and SAIF provides regional access to high-end instruments.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive infrastructure-purpose pairs and complete the code.
accepted.sec: DST facility programmes - full forms and purpose

accepted.s: NIDHI, launched in 2016, is an initiative of which department?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
accepted.x: NIDHI, or National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, was launched in 2016 by the Department of Science and Technology.
accepted.tq: Direct scheme-and-department recall.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a component associated with NIDHI?
accepted.x: NIDHI includes PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, Technology Business Incubators, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is a separate startup-support programme associated with NCGTC.
accepted.tq: Find the programme component belonging to another startup scheme.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

accepted.s: PRAYAS under NIDHI is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: PRAYAS is the NIDHI component that provides grants for prototyping. NIDHI also includes EIR, seed support, incubators, accelerators and Centres of Excellence.
accepted.tq: Component-purpose matching.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

accepted.s:
The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme is administered by DPIIT and provides funding for:
1. Proof of concept
2. Prototyping
3. Market entry
4. Regional access to high-end analytical instruments
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme supports proof of concept, prototyping and market entry. Regional access to high-end analytical instruments is the purpose of SAIF, not SISFS.
accepted.tq: Separate startup financing purposes from DST facility purposes.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

accepted.s: Which organisation is associated with the Fund of Funds for Startups involving ₹10,000 crore?
accepted.x: The Fund of Funds for Startups, involving ₹10,000 crore, is associated with SIDBI. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is associated with NCGTC.
accepted.tq: Agency-and-amount discrimination between two startup finance mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

accepted.s: TIDE 2.0 is correctly described as:
o: Training Initiative for Digital Enterprises, implemented by DBT for biotechnology scientists
Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs, implemented by MeitY to support ICT and technology start-ups through incubators
Technology Innovation and Development of Education, implemented by DPIIT for school students
Technology Infrastructure Development for Education, implemented by DST for universities
accepted.x: TIDE 2.0 stands for Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs. It is a MeitY programme launched in 2019 to support ICT and technology start-ups through incubators.
accepted.tq: Full-form, ministry and target-sector discrimination.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

accepted.s:
Arrange the following initiatives in chronological order of their launch or beginning:
A. TIDE 2.0
B. NIDHI
C. INSPIRE
D. Swarnajayanti Fellowship
accepted.x: The correct order is Swarnajayanti Fellowship (1997), INSPIRE (2008), NIDHI (2016), and TIDE 2.0 (2019).
accepted.tq: Use the first and last dates, then place the two middle initiatives.
accepted.sec: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0
